note: The small case and the reduction to binary Goldbach on n-p match; the prime p comes from the kernel-checked Proth ladder (window width <4e18) instead of a prime-gap bound with Delta, and n-4 is not bounded via (n-4)/Delta. Lean's small case uses p=3 explicitly.

snippet.text:
by_cases hsmall : n ≤ 4 * 10 ^ 18 + 3
  · -- `n = 3 + (n − 3)`
    have hev : Even (n - 3) := Nat.Odd.sub_odd hn (by decide)
    obtain ⟨p, q, hp, hq, hpq⟩ := hBG (n - 3) hev (by obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hn; omega) (by omega)
    exact ⟨3, p, q, Nat.prime_three, hp, hq, by omega⟩

proof_context.conclusion: For odd n<=4e18+3, n=3+(n-3) with n-3 even a sum of two primes by binary Goldbach.

· -- a prime `p ∈ [n − 4·10¹⁸, n − 4]` from rung `i` of the ladder
    push Not at hsmall
    have hi1 : 1 ≤ (n - 5) / 3927138875067072512 := by omega
    have hi2 : (n - 5) / 3927138875067072512 ≤ 254638308 := by omega
    obtain ⟨p, hp, hp1, hp2⟩ := Ladder.ladder_prime hi1 hi2
    have hpb : p ≤ n - 4 := by omega
    have hpa : n - 4 * 10 ^ 18 ≤ p := by omega
    have hp2' : p ≠ 2 := by omega
    have hpo : Odd p := hp.odd_of_ne_two hp2'
    have hev : Even (n - p) := Nat.Odd.sub_odd hn hpo
    obtain ⟨q, r, hq, hr, hqr⟩ := hBG (n - p) hev (by omega) (by omega)

proof_context.conclusion: For larger n takes a ladder prime p in [n-4e18, n-4], n-p even in [4,4e18], and applies binary Goldbach to n-p.
